**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed).

The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation obligation in either direction. Multiple phrasing searches ("most favored nation", "no less favorable", "favourable/favorable", "best price", "match", "first refusal", "other customers") returned nothing responsive.

The closest provision is Section 18.4 (p0255), which requires only that M&I "have the opportunity to bid on and be considered for" Customer technology projects. That is a right to be considered — it does not oblige Tri City to give M&I terms no less favourable than those offered to third parties, nor to match competing bids, so it does not trigger the MFN rule (any concern there belongs under exclusivity/right-to-bid review).

This sits at the playbook's preferred position: no MFN obligation burdening the Customer.
